s: A multinational insurance company is deploying an internal claims processing AI assistant that is powered by Amazon Bedrock FMs. The AI assistant must use several internal APIs to retrieve claim records, perform fraud checks, and update policy dat a. The company already exposes the APIs through a centralized Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway where enterprise policies enforce IAM authorization, request validation, and tool-level access controls. Some specialized validation logic for claims processing runs in containerized microservices. During inference, the company wants the FMs to automatically discover and invoke only approved tools that are exposed through the enterprise integration layer. The company does not want to implement any application-side orchestration loop to run tools. Which solution will meet these requirements?
o: Register AgentCore Runtime service endpoints as tools in the Amazon Bedrock Responses API so that Amazon Bedrock automatically discovers available tools that the company hosts in AgentCore Runtime.
Configure the Responses API to reference the AgentCore gateway ARN as the tool connector so the model retrieves and invokes the catalog of approved tools.
Establish an MCP connection between Amazon Bedrock and an AgentCore Runtime cluster to allow the AI assistant to invoke Runtime services.
Configure AgentCore Runtime services as Amazon Bedrock action groups. Invoke the action groups through the InvokeModelWithResponseStream API during FM inference.
e: B is correct because Amazon Bedrock supports server-side tool execution through AgentCore Gateway integration with the Responses API. The key requirement is that the model must discover and invoke only approved tools from the centralized enterprise integration layer without a client-side orchestration loop. AWS states that customers can specify an AgentCore Gateway ARN as a tool connector in Responses API requests. Bedrock then discovers tools from the gateway, presents them during inference, executes selected tool calls server-side, and injects results automatically. AgentCore Runtime is for hosting agents or tools, but the question already says approved APIs are exposed through AgentCore Gateway. Action groups are part of Bedrock Agents, not the direct Responses API server-side gateway connector pattern.

w.y: The deciding words are 'automatically discover and invoke only approved tools' through the existing gateway and 'no application-side orchestration loop'. Pointing the Bedrock Responses API at the AgentCore Gateway as a tool connector lets the model list and call the gateway's governed tools server side.

o.A: Runtime endpoints are not registered as discoverable tools in the Responses API, and this bypasses the gateway's policies.
o.B: Correct: use the AgentCore gateway as the tool connector so the model gets the approved tool catalog.
o.C: Connecting to Runtime directly skips the gateway where authorization and tool-level controls live.
o.D: Action groups belong to Bedrock Agents and are not called through InvokeModelWithResponseStream; that would still need your own loop.
